tip: ли turns a statement into a yes/no question and attaches to the word being asked about: Правда ли (pravda li = is it true).
Imperfective future is буду/будешь (budu/budesh) plus an infinitive; the verb itself does not change: буду есть (budu yest = will eat).
After когда about the future, Russian keeps future tense where English uses present: когда будете уходить (kogda budete ukhodit = when you leave).
Быть (byt) has no present-tense form, but its future is regular: всё будет хорошо (vsyo budet khorosho = all will be fine).
A singular informal command takes the present-tense stem and adds -и (-i): переведёшь (perevedyosh) becomes Переведи (perevedi = translate).
A plural or polite command ends in -ите (-ite): Отдохните (otdokhnite = rest). Drop the -те (-te) for one close friend.
Давай plus a perfective we-form makes a let's suggestion: Давай встретимся (davay vstretimsya = let's meet).
A comparative followed by a bare genitive means than, with no separate word for it: холоднее осени (kholodneye oseni = colder than autumn).
бы plus a past-tense verb means would; бы never changes, the verb carries gender and number: бы выучили (by vyuchili = would learn).
следовало бы plus an infinitive means should or ought to: следовало бы подождать (sledovalo by podozhdat = ought to wait).
кто (kto) becomes кого when it is the object (whom): Кого бы ты пригласил (kogo by ty priglasil = whom would you invite).
In conditionals the past verb still shows gender: была бы (byla by = would be, feminine); a man would say был бы (byl by).
A short passive participle works like is done and agrees with its subject in gender: уже сделана (uzhe sdelana = is already done), feminine.
Use где for where pointing at a place, marking location rather than motion: Ресторан, где (restoran, gde = the restaurant where).
пользоваться (polzovatsya) takes the instrumental, so which appears as которым: телефон, которым я пользуюсь (telefon, kotorym ya polzuyus = the phone I use).
который (kotoryy) agrees with its noun in gender and number, but its case comes from its own clause: в которой (v kotoroy = in which), feminine, prepositional after в.
на моём месте is the set phrase for in my place: на моём месте (na moyom meste = if I were you). месте is prepositional after на.
Unreal conditionals put бы in both halves: Если бы ты спросил, я бы ответил (yesli by ty sprosil, ya by otvetil = if you had asked, I would have answered).
As ... as is такой же plus an adjective plus как: такой же большой, как (takoy zhe bolshoy, kak = as big as).
свой (svoy) means one's own and points back to the subject, replacing мой (moy) or его (yego) when they equal the doer: своё имя (svoyo imya = your own name).
ближе pairs with к plus the dative to say closer to: ближе к школе (blizhe k shkole = closer to school).
Было бы plus an adjective plus an infinitive makes an impersonal it would be: Было бы полезно (bylo by polezno = it would be useful).
Superlatives use самый (samyy) before the adjective, both agreeing with the noun: Самая холодная зима (samaya kholodnaya zima = the coldest winter), feminine.
на plus an amount tells you by how much with a comparative: старше на два года (starshe na dva goda = older by two years).
кто counts as singular, so its verb stays singular even after plural Те: Те, кто опоздал (te, kto opozdal = those who were late).
Russian doubles the negative, ни plus a second negator не: ни с чем не сравнить (ni s chem ne sravnit = cannot be compared to anything).
Negative commands normally use the imperfective verb: Не трогай (ne trogay = don't touch), not the perfective тронь (tron).
всё before a comparative means more and more: всё выше и выше (vsyo vyshe i vyshe = higher and higher).
та (ta) becomes той in the genitive of comparison: не легче той (ne legche toy = no easier than that one), feminine matching задача (zadacha).
из plus the genitive means out of and mirrors в (v) plus accusative for going in: из дома (iz doma = out of the house).
The person receiving something goes in the dative: Передай мне (pereday mne = pass me). мне is the dative of я (ya).
